# Per-app notes

## syncthing / app-syncthing

- `syncthing` chart = one instance per release (every resource id `main`, resources generated by `templates/_feature.tpl` like the postgresql chart). Needs `user` and `global.domain`. UI at `<user>.syncthing.<domain>` through the shared Gateway + ExternalAuth. Rootless uid 1000, `STNODEFAULTFOLDER=1`, probes `/rest/noauth/health` on 8384, egress only to the relay on 22067.
- `app-syncthing` = relay + one HelmRelease `syncthing-<user>` per `global.lldapUsers` entry in group `app_syncthing` (id must be a DNS label). Its `loader.yaml` uses the feature-merge pattern (include feature, `fromYaml`, `mustMergeOverwrite` into `.Values`, `renderResources`).
- Relay (`syncthing-relay`): `docker.io/syncthing/relaysrv`, `command: [/bin/strelaysrv]` (the image entrypoint needs root), args `-keys=/var/strelaysrv -pools= -status-srv= -token=$(RELAY_TOKEN)`, rootless + read-only rootfs verified. Public through a ListenerSet TCP listener 22067 + TCPRoute. Secrets from `syncthing-pre`: StringSecret token and a cert-manager Certificate (self-signed, ECDSA 256, `rotationPolicy: Never`: the relay ID is a hash of the certificate).
- Instances self-configure through a sidecar `relay-config` (script in a ConfigMap; pod restart on change comes from the checksum mutation): computes the relay ID from the public cert, reads the API key from `config.xml`, PATCHes `/rest/config/options` `listenAddresses = relay://syncthing-relay:22067/?id=<id>&token=<tok>`; loop 2 s then 30 s (UI edits reverted). A wrong token gives a relay listener restart loop and never "Joined relay". The token lands in `config.xml` and logs (unavoidable).
- Remote peers use `relay://<public dns of the Gateway IP>:22067/?id=<id>&token=<token>` (DNS is a manual step).

## seafile

Seafile CE 13 (`seafile-mc`) + mariadb (own HelmRelease) + valkey. Runs as root with caps `CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETGID, SETUID, KILL, NET_BIND_SERVICE` (dropping all breaks nginx chown). Required env: `SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_{CCNET,SEAFILE,SEAHUB}_DB_NAME`, `REDIS_PORT` (else no redis), `JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` >= 32 chars, `enableServiceLinks: false`. OAuth through a ConfigMap `local_settings.py` symlinked into the seahub dir by the container command (uses `$SEAFILE_VERSION`).

## paperless

paperless-ngx + CloudNativePG (`sslmode=require` via `PAPERLESS_DB_OPTIONS`) + valkey. Rootless uid/gid 1000, fsGroup 1000, drop ALL. Probes need a `Host: localhost` header (`PAPERLESS_URL` sets `ALLOWED_HOSTS`); `/` returns 302 which is healthy.

## tuwunel + element

Tuwunel (Matrix, RocksDB, no postgres): all config through `TUWUNEL_<OPTION>` env (`__` for tables, IdP = `TUWUNEL_IDENTITY_PROVIDER__0__<FIELD>`); validate with `TUWUNEL_ERROR_ON_UNKNOWN_CONFIG_OPTS=true`. `server_name` is immutable, federation disabled. Element is vouched with `TUWUNEL_OIDC_REGISTRATION_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS`. Element image: user nginx (101), `ELEMENT_WEB_PORT=8080`, read-only rootfs needs writable `/tmp` and `/etc/nginx/conf.d` (emptyDir), config at `/app/config.json`. Docker `--tmpfs` is root-owned: add `:uid=101,gid=101` when testing non-root.

## sftp (app-sftp, image `docker/alpine/alpine-sftp`)

- sshd `AuthenticationMethods publickey,keyboard-interactive:pam`; PAM module `Nithe14/pam_oauth2_device` (Rust, built in the Dockerfile, must be installed in `/usr/lib/security`, not `/lib`: "Module is unknown" otherwise).
- Users: `app.lldapUsers` in group `app_sftp` with a custom lldap attribute `sshpublickey` become ConfigMap lines `<id> <uid> <key>` (uid = 20000 + adler32 % 40000); accounts are created at pod start; chroot `/data/<user>`, writable `/files`.
- Exposure: SSH over TLS on `<host>:443` by SNI. nginx is a sidecar in the pod (8443 -> 127.0.0.1:22), certificate created in the `-pre` release, TLSRoute backend = Service 443 -> 8443, host key = cert-manager ECDSA never rotated. Needs egress to authelia through `toFQDNs` (see gateway-api.md).
- Verified in docker only (image builds, sshd starts with SYS_CHROOT/SETUID/SETGID, key accepted, PAM calls the IdP). Not verified: real device flow, TLS wrapper.

## jellyfin + seerr

- Jellyfin SSO plugin `9p4/jellyfin-plugin-sso` (archived, pinned version, md5 verified) installed by an init container into `/config/plugins/...`; a `configure` sidecar (node script in ConfigMap `jellyfin-scripts`) completes the wizard, POSTs `/sso/OID/Add/authelia`, sets the branding disclaimer, loops hourly.
- The admin password is generated in `jellyfin-pre` (secret `jellyfin-admin`); seerr copies it with a SecretStore (`jellyfin-reader` ServiceAccount, Role in the jellyfin namespace). A previously generated secret owned by secret-generator must be deleted for external-secrets to take over.
- Seerr self-configures (init container `configure` writes `settings.json` at each start: completes the jellyfin wizard if needed, creates API key, libraries, `main.mediaServerType=2`, `public.initialized=true`, OIDC provider; sets `discoverRegion`/`streamingRegion`, missing fields crash its migrations). The first admin login `/auth/jellyfin` sets `settings.jellyfin.ip` from `body.hostname` and rejects a hostname when `ip` is already set: keep `ip: ''` until the marker `/app/config/.admin-created` exists (a sidecar posts the login with the hostname, then writes the marker).
- Media over SFTP: `app-csi-rclone` (veloxpack chart, group `extra`) with a `-pre` release providing known_hosts ConfigMap, StorageClass `rclone-sftp` and a Kyverno mutation adding `skipPodRestrictHostAccess`. The media PVC (ReadOnlyMany) needs an admin secret with the rclone INI (`key_pem` with `\n`, `shell_type = none`, `known_hosts_file`). Nodes must reach the storage host's sshd directly (no ProxyCommand in rclone). Resources of `-pre` releases are not in the app golden: verify with `helm template` of `base-loader` plus the values from the golden.

## valkey chart

Wraps the public valkey chart through an OCI dependency (`oci://ghcr.io/valkey-io/valkey-helm`, Flux resolves it) plus a base feature: StringSecret `main` (one key per `valkey.auth.aclUsers` user) and CNP `main` from `clients`. Needs `checkRequiredValues: false`. Apps use a sub-HelmRelease `<app>-valkey` (chart `./kube/charts/valkey`, `dependsOn` app-secret-generator); the release name must contain `valkey`. When resources move between Helm releases, an ownership error self-heals after the old release drops them (the password is regenerated: cache and sessions only).

## firefox-sync

Mozilla `syncstorage-rs` postgres image, amd64 only (nodeSelector on arch), uid 10001, port 8000. Storage and tokenserver share one CNPG database, no TLS; the DB URL uses `$(DB_PASSWORD)` so that variable must sort before `SYNC_*`. Auth = Mozilla accounts (egress to the accounts host), no OIDC, no forward auth. `SYNC_TOKENSERVER__ALLOW_NEW_USERS` true until devices are registered.

## mailu

- Dovecot FTS (flatcurve): active index at `/mail/<user>/[.<folder>/]fts-flatcurve/{index.N,current.N}`; `xapian-indexes/db_*` is a legacy unused layout. Crash loop `Xapian::DatabaseCorruptError`: find the mailbox with `doveadm fts-flatcurve stats -u <user> <mailbox>` (aborts on the bad one), `xapian-check <shard>` (rc 1 = corrupt), fix with `doveadm fts-flatcurve remove -u <user> <mailbox>`.
- Policies needed: dovecot -> tika:9998 (+ ingress on tika), front -> postfix:25 and 10025 (authenticated submission).
- Write multi-step shell scripts to a file and read output from a file when the terminal output is polluted by history.

## edge (app-edge) and the NixOS module `bcl.edge` / role `edge`

Entry of a cluster from the internet through the edge nodes, no router in the path, client address kept. An edge node is a NixOS VPS with no cluster of its own: the service is the module `bcl.edge` (`nixos/modules/nixos/bcl/edge.nix`: WireGuard `wg-edge`, its private key derived from the SSH host key (X25519, as `ssh-to-age`, never stored), haproxy owning 80/443: TLS and HTTP forwarded as they are, `send-proxy-v2 source <tunnel address>` to the cluster, optional Postfix relay), usable next to other roles as long as 80/443 are free and the firewall is on; the role `edge` (`bcl.role.name = "edge"`, `role/edge.nix`) enables it and sets the VPS around it (DHCP on the NIC, firewall, encrypted disk with initrd SSH). Cluster: pod with a `wireguard` container (`ip link add wg0 type wireguard`, one `wg set` peer per pop, the pod dials, keepalive 25) and a haproxy (`accept-proxy` on 8080/8443 for the tunnel, plain 9080/9443 for the LAN and the pods, both `send-proxy-v2` to `cilium-gateway-shared.cilium.svc`).

- Cilium `gatewayAPI.enableProxyProtocol` is global to the Gateway listeners: once on, only PROXY connections are accepted. So the pod also takes the LoadBalancer IP of the Gateway (LAN and in-cluster clients) and the Gateway is moved to another address. The apps' egress rules `toEntities: [ingress]` stop matching the public names (the destination is now the pod): the chart ships a CCNP letting every pod reach the pod on 9080/9443.
- The Cilium Gateway `hostNetwork` Envoy binds 0.0.0.0:80/443 of the node: a node cannot have haproxy and that Gateway on the same ports (a specific address bind conflicts with the wildcard one too). An edge node has no Gateway: it is not in a cluster.
- Not verified on a live cluster: the egress from the pod to the Gateway ClusterIP with `toEntities: [ingress]`, `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` keeping the LAN client address through BGP, the PROXY header taken as the client address by the Gateway. Verified: the chart golden and inner render, the edge node NixOS evaluation, `haproxy -c` of the generated config.
- Mail (`tcp`, `relay`): the edge nodes forward `upstream.tcpPorts` with `send-proxy-v2` to the pod on `port + tcpPortOffset` (10000), which sends the PROXY header straight to the `backend` service (`tcp.<name>.backend`, not through the Gateway): the server must read it from the pod only (stalwart: `overrideProxyTrustedNetworks` of its mail listeners, set by the `setup.plan` of app-stalwart). The outgoing mails go to the Service `edge-relay:2525`, haproxy sends them through the tunnel to the postfix of an edge node (`bcl.edge.relay`, listens on the tunnel address only, `relay.hostname` must be the reverse DNS of the edge node).
- Gateway `enableProxyProtocol: true` is enough: `useRemoteAddress` stays at its default (true), the downstream address of the PROXY header is then the client one and goes to `X-Forwarded-For`. The forward auth does not get `X-Forwarded-For`.
- haproxy 3.x refuses a frontend and a backend with the same name; the servers of the `tcp` services use `resolvers ... init-addr none` (the service may not exist yet), `haproxy -c` of the golden fails offline only on the unresolved `cilium-gateway-shared.cilium.svc`.

## stalwart-setup (app-stalwart)

Settings of Stalwart live in its database: the CronJob `stalwart-setup` (release disabled by default, `resources.fluxHelmReleases.stalwart-setup.enabled: true` in the cluster values) applies `setup.plan` (a list of CLI plan operations, one JSON object each, idempotent: `upsert` with `matchOn`, `update` of singletons) with the distroless image `ghcr.io/stalwartlabs/cli` (arguments only, no shell; `STALWART_USER=admin` + the password of `stalwart-admin`, nothing in git). An init container applies, the container restarts Stalwart when the hash of the plan is not the annotation `bcl.tf/stalwart-setup-plan` of the Deployment (listeners are read at start). A run fails until Stalwart has been set up in the web UI, the next one works. Not tested against a live server: the object and field names come from the docs (NetworkListener `overrideProxyTrustedNetworks` as `{cidr: true}`, MtaRoute `@type: Relay`, MtaOutboundStrategy `route`, Action `ReloadSettings`), check with `stalwart-cli apply --dry-run` and `describe`.
